description:
Writes a whole structure of thoughts, links, notes and tags in a single call. Call it once you have decomposed some material (an article, a document, a discussion) into several connected thoughts — creating them one by one at that volume is slow and breaks halfway.
Thoughts reference each other by tempId, arbitrary labels you invent yourself; the server substitutes real identifiers. A parent may be either a tempId from this batch or the UUID of an existing thought, which is how a new branch grafts onto what the brain already holds.
Search with brain_search first: some of the thoughts may already exist, and linking to them beats creating duplicates.

brainId.description: Brain identifier. Take it from brain_list — never guess it.

deduplicate.description: Skip creating a thought when the same parent already has a child with that name. On by default, which makes re-running a batch safe.

links.description: Extra links on top of the hierarchy. These are what turn a set of thoughts into a graph — use them freely and label them.

thoughts.description: The batch's thoughts. Order does not matter; dependencies resolve themselves.

parent.description: A tempId from this batch or the UUID of an existing thought. Without it the thought is left unlinked.

relation.description: How this thought relates to its parent. Usually child.

tempId.description: Label for references within this batch, e.g. "rag" or "t1".

name: brain_ingest
